Use this to refer to the current object.

body.en: A *constructor* is a member with the same name as its class and no return type (not even void). It is called automatically when an object is created with new, and it initialises the instance variables. If a class has no constructor, Java supplies a default constructor that sets numbers to 0, booleans to false and references to null. A parameterised constructor takes arguments: new Student("Asha", 12). Constructors can be overloaded like methods.

body.en: Inside an instance method or constructor, this is a reference to the current object, the object on which the method was called. It is used to tell a field from a parameter with the same name (this.roll = roll), to pass the current object to another method, and to call another constructor of the same class from the first line of a constructor: this(0, "unknown"). Static methods have no this, because they are not called on an object.

points.en: this.x = x separates field from parameter
this(...) calls another constructor (first line only)
